newsitem.title: USA: Arbor says CBOT 1996 volume seen a record.
newsitem.headline: Arbor says CBOT 1996 volume seen a record.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) chairman Patrick Arbor said CBOT volume will likely climb to a record 225 million contracts for 1996.
"I think we'll trade probably 225 million contracts," Arbor said at luncheon to European journalists, noting that total volume for both financial and agricultural products rose six percent this year.
Total volume in 1995 was 210.7 million contracts. The record, prior to this year, was set in 1994 at 219.5 million contracts.
From January to September 1996, total volume increased 5.9 percent to 170,487,642 contracts from 161,026,010 contracts in the same period a year earlier, according to the CBOT.
At the luncheon, Arbor noted that for the first nine months of 1996, agricultural trading volume was up 43 percent from a year ago. Volume for agricultural options rose 89 percent.

"What's critical is that our ag options volume is up 89 percent -- almost 90 percent -- so it's up almost twice as much as our futures volume," Arbor said. "You can see that the growth is really in options." -Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
